newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian stocks soar on BNI listing.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian stocks soar on BNI listing.

text.p: Giant state-owned Bank Negara Indonesia (BNI) was listed locally on Monday after one of the country's best-received floats, propelling turnover to near-record levels and sending the index surging.
The index closed 2.51 percent higher at 628.24 points on a sharp inflow of funds following the listing of BNI, brokers said.

"It was widely expected that the BNI listing would enliven Jakarta stocks. I think it (the boom) will last until the second week of December before the market slows down for the Christmas holiday," a foreign broker said.
Brokers said that strong buying interest in BNI had sparked extremely positive sentiment and also triggered a rise in other banking stocks and issues with sound fundamentals.
"Some fresh funds came into the market and fundamentally sound and liquid stocks benefited," an analyst from a Hong Kong-based securities firm said.
BNI closed at 1,250 rupiah against an offer price of 850 rupiah and topped the active list with a staggering 179.33 million shares traded. It had risen to 1,300 rupiah earlier.
BNI accounted for more than half the shares traded on the exchange on Monday. The turnover is the among the highest ever recorded in Jakarta, exchange officials said.
A total of 4.34 billion BNI shares were listed on the Jakarta and Surabaya stock exchanges on Monday.
